images.title: One whole, two parts
images.purpose: Show that three numbers, one whole and two parts, give four sentences: two additions and two subtractions.
images.composition: A bar for 63 split into 35 and 28 with the four sentences under it.
images.exact_structure: Plain white frame, 1456 by 816. A bar split into two parts, and four sentences. The WHOLE BAR is a rectangle x 150 to 1306, y 150 to 260 (1156 by 110 px), outlined dark #2B2B2B 3 px, filled pale grey #D9D9D9, with the number 63 in dark #1F2937 bold sans-serif (84 px) centred inside it. Under it, the same width split in two PARTS, y 290 to 400: the left part x 150 to 792 filled teal #0072B2 with the number 35 in dark #1F2937 bold sans-serif (84 px) centred inside, the right part x 792 to 1306 filled amber #E69F00 with the number 28 in dark #1F2937 bold sans-serif (84 px) centred inside, both outlined dark 3 px. Below, four rounded rectangles outlined dark 3 px, 550 by 80 px, in two columns: x 150 to 700 and x 756 to 1306; rows y 480 to 560 and y 600 to 680. Their text in dark #1F2937 bold sans-serif (56 px) centred: first row 35 + 28 = 63 (left) and 28 + 35 = 63 (right); second row 63 − 28 = 35 (left) and 63 − 35 = 28 (right). No other text. Nothing else in the frame.

images.takeaway: The whole minus a part is the other part, and the two parts added make the whole.
images.description: A bar 63 split into 35 and 28, with the sentences 35 + 28 = 63, 28 + 35 = 63, 63 − 28 = 35 and 63 − 35 = 28.
images.context: Concept image for Subtraction: the Link with Addition and Place Value, Section A, using the example's own numbers (practice values).
images.teaching_notes: Point at the whole and then at each part. The slip to watch: thinking addition and subtraction are unrelated.

images.title: Subtract 38 from 72
images.purpose: Show subtraction with place value: 1 ten is regrouped as 10 ones when there are too few ones.
images.composition: A tens and ones chart for 72 − 38 with the regroup marks 6 and 12, the difference 34 and a small check line.
images.exact_structure: Plain white frame, 1456 by 816. A place value chart, 2 columns each 240 px wide, x 488 to 968. Column header row y 70 to 140 with the names Tens, Ones in dark #1F2937 bold sans-serif (38 px), each centred in its column. The chart body is a table with 1 header row and 4 rows, outlined dark #2B2B2B 3 px, with thin construction grey #6B7280 lines (2 px) between the columns. Row 1 (carry row) y 140 to 215; row 2 (first number) y 215 to 315; row 3 (second number) y 315 to 415; a thick dark rule (6 px) at y 425 across the chart; row 4 (answer row) y 435 to 535. In the first number row (centre y 265) the digits, left to right, are: 7 at x 608; 2 at x 848, each in dark #1F2937 bold sans-serif (84 px). In the second number row (centre y 365) the digits, left to right, are: 3 at x 608; 8 at x 848, each in dark #1F2937 bold sans-serif (84 px). In the answer row (centre y 485) the digits, left to right, are: 3 at x 608; 4 at x 848, each in dark #1F2937 bold sans-serif (84 px). A − sign in dark #1F2937 bold sans-serif (84 px) stands at x 428, y 365, to the left of the second number. In the carry row there are exactly 2 circles: a circle of 64 px diameter outlined green #009E73 (4 px) at x 608, y 178 holding 6; a circle of 64 px diameter outlined green #009E73 (4 px) at x 848, y 178 holding 12. The circle over the Tens column holds 6, the circle over the Ones column holds 12, and each of the two top digits (7 and 2) has a diagonal construction grey line (4 px) struck through it.  Under the chart, centred at x 728, y 650, the line 72 − 38 = 34 in dark #1F2937 bold sans-serif (96 px), the largest text in the frame. Under it, centred at x 728, y 740, the secondary line check: 38 + 34 = 72 in construction grey #6B7280 bold sans-serif (44 px), clearly smaller than the main line. No other text. Nothing else in the frame.

images.takeaway: Regroup 1 ten as 10 ones: 12 − 8 = 4 and 6 − 3 = 3, so 72 − 38 = 34.
images.description: A chart with 72 above 38, the regroup marks 6 and 12 over the struck digits, the difference 34 and the check 38 + 34 = 72.
images.context: Concept image for Subtraction: the Link with Addition and Place Value, Section B, using the example's own numbers (practice values).
images.teaching_notes: Show where the 1 ten went: the 7 became 6 and the 2 became 12. Then check by adding 38 and 34. The slip to watch: taking the smaller digit from the bigger.

image_decisions.why: One video, two sections, one picture each: the bar shows the whole and its two parts for Section A, and the chart with its regroup marks shows subtracting with place value for Section B.
